# COIN (Coinbase Global, Inc.): Technical Analysis as of 2026-11-23

## 1. Summary

COIN is in a steep, persistent downtrend. Every trend indicator is bearish, and momentum is near oversold but has not turned. The 2026-11-23 close of **108.78** is a small bounce from the 2026-11-20 close of 101.97. The data does not yet show whether this is a durable reversal or a pause inside a falling market.

Unless noted, figures come from the verified snapshot. The indicator-tool outputs matched it where both reported a value, so I found no conflicts.

## 2. Indicators selected and why

These eight are complementary and cover different questions:

| Role | Indicator | Why it fits this market |
|---|---|---|
| Short-term trend | close_10_ema | Tracks the fast momentum shift in a sharp decline |
| Medium-term trend | close_50_sma | Dynamic resistance and trend filter |
| Long-term trend | close_200_sma | Strategic regime and cross confirmation |
| Momentum/trend change | macd (with macds, macdh from the snapshot) | Shows whether downside momentum is accelerating or fading |
| Overbought/oversold | rsi | Flags stretched conditions after a rapid decline |
| Volatility/extremes | boll_lb (with boll, boll_ub from the snapshot) | Shows where price sits relative to the volatility envelope |
| Risk sizing | atr | Sets stop distance and position size |
| Volume-weighted trend | vwma | Checks whether volume confirms the price move |

## 3. Price action and context

- **Recent range:** From the data pulled (2026-05-26 to 2026-11-23), the highest daily high was **208.33** on 2026-09-21. The lowest low was **101.71** on 2026-11-20. Price is now well below the entire prior range, since the earlier lows were around 139–141 (for example 139.11 on 2026-07-31 and 139.18 on 2026-06-26).
- **Breakdown on 2026-10-30:** Close fell from 160.59 to **143.54** on about 20.9M shares. That is one of the heaviest-volume days in the sample, and it started the current leg down.
- **Pattern since then:** The closes show lower highs and lower lows. An attempted rebound on 2026-11-03 and 2026-11-04 (145.45, then 151.50) failed the next day with a drop to 136.82. Later bounces were smaller, such as 136.27 on 2026-11-11.
- **Acceleration:** From 2026-11-13 (127.65) through 2026-11-20 (101.97), COIN closed lower on every session. The 2026-11-20 low-of-range day came on about 14.1M shares.
- **Latest session (2026-11-23):** Open 109.56, high 111.40, low 107.20, close 108.78, volume 10,729,777. The close is up from 101.97, but the session opened about 7.6 above the prior close, so the bounce began with a gap up. The volume figure may be partial if the session was still in progress, so treat it cautiously.

## 4. Trend indicators

- **10 EMA: 117.94.** Price is below it. The EMA has fallen every trading day shown (170.77 on 2026-10-26 to 117.94 now). It is the first resistance reference for a rebound. A close back above it would be the first sign of short-term improvement.
- **50 SMA: 162.14.** It has fallen from about 180.3 on 2026-10-29. Price is roughly 53 below it, so it is far from relevant for now.
- **200 SMA: 172.17.** It is also declining, from 180.07 on 2026-10-26. Price is roughly 63 below it.
- **Death cross:** Per the tool output, the 50 SMA was still above the 200 SMA on 2026-11-05 (176.47 vs 176.43). It crossed below on 2026-11-06 (175.35 vs 175.99). The gap has widened since, to 162.14 vs 172.17. This is a lagging confirmation of a trend that was already in place, not a leading signal.
- **Stack order:** Price (108.78) < 10 EMA (117.94) < 50 SMA (162.14) < 200 SMA (172.17). This is a fully bearish alignment.
- **VWMA: 124.39.** This figure comes from the indicator tool only. The snapshot does not list it, so I did not cross-verify it. It is above price and below the 20-period Bollinger middle (133.09). That suggests heavier volume has traded at lower prices, which is consistent with the selling being volume-backed. VWMA has been falling in step with the other averages.

## 5. Momentum

- **MACD: -15.85, signal -13.79, histogram -2.06 (signal and histogram from the snapshot).** The MACD line is below both the signal line and zero, so momentum is bearish.
- **MACD trend:** The line was -4.36 on 2026-10-26 and reached about -15.89 on 2026-11-20. The 2026-11-23 reading (-15.85) is marginally higher, so downside momentum has stopped accelerating. The histogram is still negative, though, and no bullish crossover has occurred.
- **RSI: 29.80.** It reached **22.94** on 2026-11-20 and has recovered to just under the 30 oversold threshold. RSI has been at or below about 40 since 2026-10-30, which is typical of a persistent downtrend. In such trends RSI can stay oversold for extended periods.
- **Divergence:** I do not see bullish divergence in the data. RSI made a lower low (22.94) alongside the lower price low, and MACD made a lower low as well. Momentum has confirmed the price weakness, not diverged from it.

## 6. Volatility and risk

- **Bollinger Bands:** The lower band is 96.82, the middle is 133.09, and the upper is 169.35. The bands have widened and shifted down with the move. The lower band was 160.44 on 2026-10-26 and is 96.82 now. On 2026-11-20 the close (101.97) and the low (101.71) both stayed above that day's lower band (99.41), so price did not close outside the band. Price is now roughly 12 above the lower band and far below the middle band.
- **ATR: 9.07.** This is about 8% of the current price, which is very high. It peaked near 11.06 on 2026-11-05 and has eased since, even as price fell, which points to a steady grind lower more than a series of explosive days.
- **Sizing example:** A 1.5×ATR stop is about 13.6, and a 2×ATR stop is about 18.1. Daily swings of that size are normal here, so tight stops risk being hit by noise.

## 7. Scenarios the data supports

- **Bearish continuation:** A close back below 101.97 (the 2026-11-20 close) or a break of the 101.71 low would extend the sequence of lower lows. The Bollinger lower band at 96.82 is the next volatility reference, not a proven support level.
- **Relief bounce:** A rebound would first meet the 10 EMA (117.94), then the VWMA (124.39), then the 20-period middle band (133.09). Failure at the falling 10 EMA would be consistent with a bounce inside the downtrend. The 50 SMA (162.14) and 200 SMA (172.17) are far away.
- **Signs of a real bottom (not yet present):** A close above the 10 EMA, a MACD histogram turning positive or a MACD/signal crossover, and RSI rising back above 30 and holding. None of these has happened.

## 8. Limitations

- I did not test whether any level has acted as support or resistance historically, so the reference levels above are not backed by tested bounces.
- The VWMA and the 2026-11-23 volume are not independently verified. The volume may reflect an incomplete session.
- This is a technical read only. It does not include news, fundamentals, or crypto-market drivers, which may explain the sharp decline. The trade decision is left to the next agent.

At $108.78, the market cap of $28.8B is:

- about **5.3x TTM sales**, and
- about **116x annualized Q3 operating income** ($62M × 4 = $248M, a crude annualization).

Forward EPS of $2.40 implies roughly **$636M** of earnings (about 265M shares). That is about 2.5x the current operating run-rate, and it still gives a 45x forward P/E on a stock with a beta of 3.35. Those estimates were most likely set before this week's BTC repricing. For scale, each 10x of P/E on $2.40 is $24 per share. A market that gave this business 30x would put it in the $70s. That's an illustration, not a forecast.

A 62% drawdown from $284.74 says the stock got cheaper than it was. It doesn't say the stock is cheap.

## 5. Bitcoin is the whole story, and the story is getting worse

You called "the weakness is crypto-specific" a positive. It's the bear point. COIN is a crypto-volume business. And if the recession probability is 2%, there is no macro shock to reverse. A sector that keeps falling in a benign macro backdrop has its own demand problem, which is worse than a macro dip that heals with policy.

Look at the trajectory:

- Odds of BTC touching $55k rose **+18.5pp in one week to 46%**, and $50k rose to 28%. Rising odds mean the market is adding downside, not discounting it.
- BTC at $100k is 2%.
- You said "touch markets price a path." Correct, and the path is lower.
- Fed cuts are 98% off the table and market-structure legislation is at 2%. "Free optionality" at 2% is a lottery ticket, not a thesis. One StockTwits poster is already worried the legislative window closes if political control shifts. That's anecdotal, but it points the same way.
- The only equity headline in the news feed describes a "battered" market. We have only the title, so treat it as unconfirmed. With a beta of 3.35, equity weakness amplifies.
- The stock fell **20%** from 11/13 to 11/20 (127.65 → 101.97) with no company news in my data. We don't know why, which is a risk in itself.

## 6. The chart isn't capitulation, and your own points contradict each other

You said the selloff was "a grind, not a panic," then called it "capitulation." Capitulation needs panic: climactic volume followed by a reversal.

- The 11/20 low came on about 14.1M shares versus 20.9M on the 10/30 breakdown. Volume faded into the low.
- MACD going from -15.89 to -15.85 is a 0.04 change, which is noise. The technical report found **no bullish divergence**: RSI and MACD made lower lows alongside price.
- RSI at 29.80 in a trend that has held RSI below roughly 40 since 10/30 is a normal condition, not a signal.
- Staying inside the lower Bollinger band isn't support when that band fell from 160 to 97 in four weeks.
- Today's bounce hit a high of 111.40, right at the "$111 resistance" a poster flagged, and closed at 108.78, below the falling 10 EMA (117.94).
- This is the third rebound in a series of lower highs: 151.50, then 136.27, now this one.
- Today's 10.7M volume may be partial, but retail is already calling it "piss poor volume." Treat that as thin evidence.

## 7. Your 3.4:1 doesn't survive contact with the ATR

Your stop at $101.71 is $7.07 away, which is **0.78 ATR** (ATR is 9.07, about 8% of price). You said tight stops are noise-prone and then proposed one inside a single average day. This stock also gaps. It fell **-10.6% in one session** on 10/30. A stop at 101.71 doesn't cap the loss at 6.5% when the stock can open through it. The target of $133.09 sits behind three resistance layers, 117.94, 124.39 and the old $111 rejection, and the midline itself is falling. The reward-to-risk ratio only works if you get the fills, and in this tape you won't.

Your own checklist says you'd add on a close above the 10 EMA, a MACD histogram turn and RSI holding above 30. None of those has happened. So your trade is to buy before your own confirmation.

## 8. Sentiment and insiders

The sentiment sample is 18 StockTwits posts, all from one day, low confidence. It can't support "bottoms form when nobody believes the rally" any more than it supports my case. A 4.7/10 mixed reading with 46% bullish among labeled posts isn't despair.

On insiders, I agree the sales look scheduled. But the CFO sold $8.0M at about $204–207 and Andreessen sold $1.4M at $205, both on 9/21, the 6-month high. The stock is now about 47% below that. The 150-record insider feed back to June 2025 shows **no open-market buying**, not at $200 and not at $109. Silence since 10/02 is partly a function of price and trading windows, and Form 4s can lag. It isn't a vote of confidence.

## Where I could be wrong

- A BTC reversal would lift this stock hard, given the 3.35 beta. I have no spot price and no COIN news for the week, so I can't rule out a catalyst.
- Operating income could keep improving if cost cuts are structural.
- Short-covering could squeeze the stock well past my levels.

I'd change my view on a close above the falling 10 EMA, then a hold above the 124 VWMA, a positive MACD histogram, and evidence that Q4 revenue and the Q3 non-operating items support the quarter's earnings.

## Bottom line

COIN is a crypto-volume proxy with a beta of 3.35, revenue down 29% over nine months, operating income near zero, a Q3 profit that is mostly non-operating, and a 45x forward P/E that assumes a rebound no catalyst is setting up. Bitcoin downside odds are rising and no catalyst is priced. The stock is breaking a 52-week low area on lower highs, with no divergence, no climactic volume, and no insider buying. "It already fell 62%" is the line people use to justify catching knives.

My stance is to avoid it or stay underweight. If you want exposure, wait for the confirmation your own checklist demands.
